text: The Behavior section requires "No I/O except through the injected Store. No timers, no fetch, no console." notify-parlor.ts performs I/O directly: it calls console.log to print the notification and fetch to POST to an external webhook with an AbortSignal.timeout timer. All I/O must instead be routed through the injected Store (or time/randomness isolated in a single obvious place), so the service must remove the console.log and fetch calls and perform the notification via the Store.

Structure violation: the spec requires a service module to export exactly one entry point, a function named `run`. parlor.ts additionally exports `formatParlor` and `isEligible`, so it exposes three entry points. These extra exports must be moved to their own modules so the file exports only `run`.

Behavior violation: the spec requires that services do one thing and that a second responsibility becomes a second service. This module combines several responsibilities: updating a parlor's city, computing review ranking data, formatting a parlor for the digest email, and checking loyalty eligibility. These must be split into separate services.

Error messages do not meet the consumer-facing standard. "no", "opensAt failed the regex", and "closesAt failed the regex" neither name what was wrong nor state what would be accepted instead. They must be rewritten to say, e.g., "parlorId must reference an existing parlor" and "opensAt must be a time in HH:MM format".

Input is not validated before any work happens. The service computes `summary` and `label` from the input before any validation runs, and the parlor/format checks are interleaved with that work. Validation must read top-to-bottom before the happy path begins.

The service has no doc comment. Every service must have a doc comment stating its purpose in one sentence and enumerating its domain failure modes (unknown parlor, invalid opensAt, invalid closesAt) so a caller can handle every error without reading the body.
